finding.rationale: Reading sign-in logs via GET /auditLogs/signIns gives an adversary visibility into the authentication telemetry the defending team uses to detect anomalies. With the full sign-in record an adversary can identify low-detection windows (periods of low sign-in volume), correlate failed then succeeded sign-ins to infer detection thresholds, and determine which accounts generate security alerts — then operate through accounts that do not. AuditLog.Read.All is gated by the Reports Reader role or higher; restricting Reports Reader assignments to designated security operations accounts reduces the number of compromised credential paths that expose authentication telemetry to an adversary. Severity re-triaged medium -> high (2026-09-10) per docs/finding-severity-rubric-v0.1.md v1.0: the defensive-evasion escalator was adopted — a defender's-own-detection map (sign-in/alert telemetry; D=2 sub-case (b)) routes to high. Original point-in-time assessment was medium; preserved here for context.
